items.stem: An executive is choosing between AI initiatives. Which best signals a durable advantage rather than hype?

options.text: It leverages proprietary data or a hard-to-copy workflow to create lasting value
options.rationale: Correct: defensible value usually rests on assets competitors cannot easily copy.

options.text: It uses the newest model announced this month
It lets the firm say 'we use AI' in press releases
options.rationale: Marketing language is not strategic advantage.

options.text: It copies exactly what a competitor just launched

items.explanation: Correct: defensible value usually rests on assets competitors cannot easily copy.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO moves show responsible executive leadership of AI? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Define risk appetite and governance before scaling AI
options.rationale: Correct: governance set early prevents avoidable harm.

options.text: Assign clear accountability for AI outcomes
options.rationale: Correct: accountability ensures oversight and response.

options.text: Deploy widely first and consider governance later
Treat all AI risk as the vendor's problem
options.rationale: The organisation retains accountability for its use of AI.

items.explanation: Correct: governance set early prevents avoidable harm.

items.stem: Why do many AI initiatives cost more than the initial model or licence suggests?

options.text: Data, integration, talent and ongoing operation add substantial cost
options.rationale: Correct: total cost of ownership extends well beyond the model itself.

options.text: Models and licences are the only real cost
options.rationale: Operating and data costs are often larger.

options.text: AI has no ongoing operating cost
options.rationale: Running AI in production has recurring costs.

options.text: Talent is never needed for AI

items.explanation: Correct: total cost of ownership extends well beyond the model itself.
